title: AVX-512 / AVX2 Accelerated HNSW Vector Graph with Product Quantization
objective: Build a high-performance Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW) vector search index accelerated with Product Quantization (PQ) and hand-optimized SIMD intrinsics (AVX2 / AVX-512 with scalar fallback) in C++20. The engine must support incremental vector insertion, dynamic heuristic neighbor pruning (M, efConstruction, efSearch), 8-bit asymmetric distance computation (ADC) lookups, and concurrent multi-threaded k-NN queries achieving >= 95% Recall@10 on 768-dimensional vector datasets with high query throughput (QPS).
motivation: Vector similarity search powers modern semantic search, RAG retrieval pipelines, and multimodal AI. Achieving the Pareto frontier of recall vs. latency requires deep hardware-level understanding of memory cache hierarchies, prefetching, and vector SIMD instructions.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Asymmetric Distance Computation (ADC) SIMD Kernels: Implementing high-throughput distance estimation between unquantized query vectors and PQ-quantized centroids using AVX2/AVX-512 lookup and horizontal accumulation without cache line stalls.
2. Concurrent HNSW Graph Construction: Maintaining multi-layer graph connectivity, bidirectional edge updates, and entry point transitions under concurrent insertions without locks on the fast read path.
3. Heuristic Neighbor Pruning: Implementing diverse neighbor selection (Algorithm 4 in the Malkov-Yashunin HNSW paper) to prevent clustering in local graph minima and preserve recall at high compression ratios.
environmentSummary: Ubuntu 22.04 container with gcc-13, g++-13, cmake 3.28, ninja-build, valgrind, and Python 3.10 benchmark suites in /app. Pre-generated 768-dimensional normalized embedding datasets (10k train/test and 100k evaluation corpus) are bundled offline.
oracleStrategy: Reference C++20 implementation under solution/ provides an AVX2/AVX-512 SIMD-accelerated ADC distance lookup table, cache-aligned quantized codebooks, and a concurrent HNSW graph index with heuristic neighbor pruning.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh which executes four verification channels:
1. Unit & Correctness Tests (PQ training, codebook quantization, basic k-NN graph traversal).
2. Concurrent Graph Construction Stress (multi-threaded concurrent vector insertions and edge integrity validation).
3. Recall & Throughput Benchmarks (measuring Recall@10 >= 0.95 and Query Throughput >= 10,000 QPS against ground-truth exact L2 brute-force calculation on 768-dim embeddings).
4. Memory and Sanitizer Checks (AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer passes).
binarySuccessCondition: Achieves Recall@10 >= 0.92 and Throughput >= 8,000 QPS on the 768-dimensional benchmark dataset on 8 vCPUs with 0 sanitizer defects.
partialScoreStrategy: Continuous monotone score calculated as: Score = clamp((Recall - 0.70) / 0.25, 0.0, 1.0) * min(1.0, QPS / 10000.0) * 100.
anticipatedExploits:
1. Exact brute-force scan: Mathematically impossible to meet the 10,000 QPS throughput threshold on 768-dim vectors using linear brute-force scan on 8 CPUs.
2. Inverted index hacks / dimension truncation: Fails recall threshold (<0.70).
